text: #271's plumbing: a writer's retry of a plan's draft whose build failed in the factory's own run builds the ratified plan again and replaces the draft, the protocol's Rebuild (D-0202) and the recovery core's replacement (D-0203). A failure is the factory's own run's when its post records FailGate: the agent ended its last run with an error, even one that left work whose checks pass, its tests failed, or its review asked for changes. The factory checks that the protocol allows the Rebuild and finds the plan's ratification on the draft's branch first, then stores the retry's record that it replaces #N, closes #N without readying or merging it, so its work stays there to read, and answers the retry. The new build runs from that ratification on a branch of its own, named for the retry, with a run record of its own and a new review, and opens its own pull request: ready only once its checks and review pass, or a draft again, which a writer can retry in turn. Every build finds its own pull request from its branch in any state, so neither a crash nor someone's close makes it open a second, and a build a later retry replaced records its run and publishes nothing (D-0212). A draft someone merged, before the record or after it, is kept, and one someone closed before the record is theirs: either way the retry is answered without a build. A close after the record is the one the retry asked for. A retry after CI's gate failed, of a pull request that can't merge, of one waiting for a person because it changes the trusted base, of a modeled project's failed draft, or after a failure posted before failures said why, still watches it again, and one after a build that stopped still builds again, keeping the draft it replaces. The failure post, the note refusing revise, the retry's answer, the dashboard's cards, /act and the issue's history say which happens, and that a person merges a change to the trusted base. Eight pinned acceptance tests change with it, so it waits for @gitdek's ratification: #263's TestPlumbingDraftRetryPostsMatchWatching, now TestPlumbingDraftRetryPostsMatchRebuilding, and TestRejectedReviewRetrySaysAndDoesMergeTheUnchangedDraft, now TestRejectedReviewRetryRebuildsInsteadOfMergingTheDraft, expect a plan's failed draft built again; TestClippedTrustedDraftRetryKeepsClosingCommands, and TestRefusedReviseKeepsKnownTrustedBaseEvidence's trusted rejected-review case, expect the rebuild's offer, with a person merging; TestRetryCardsDescribeTheExistingAction, TestPostedRetriesSayWhetherTheyWatchOrBuild and TestRetryHistoryExplainsMergeWithoutAnotherReview expect a plan's failed draft's card to rebuild; and #251's TestClippedPostsKeepClosingCommands expects the rebuild's exact closing for a draft. Every other check in them is unchanged.
